anchor_comparisons: The positive cross-sector ordinal anchor represents sustained scarcity pricing; current utilization, constrained supply, and realized ASP gains make the direction comparable, not the industry mechanics.
The counter cross-sector ordinal anchor flags local-peak and normalization risk, but its unrelated business patterns make it ordinal rather than exact.
disagreements: I treat realized utilization and pricing as stronger than a price narrative, while discounting both cross-sector anchors as non-exact analogues.
payload.rationale: Full utilization, constrained HBM and server-DRAM supply, a mid-60% quarterly DRAM ASP increase despite flat shipments, and HBM capacity cannibalization demonstrate active pricing leverage. A through-2027 shortage view supports duration, but blended ASP is not HBM-only and competing supply can weaken scarcity.
payload.why_not_higher: Product-specific contract pricing is missing, while competing supply, HBM4 competition, and end-demand elasticity limit duration.
payload.why_not_lower: A lower placement would ignore 100% utilization, constrained supply, sharp ASP gains with flat shipments, and capacity-consumption mechanics.
